evidence.text: Cala answer: ## Seed-Stage Investments in Finnish Defence Tech Companies (Since 2024) Based on available information, here are the key seed and early-stage rounds in Finnish defence tech companies since 2024: ### 1. NestAI (Helsinki, founded 2024) - **Round:** €100 million (~$115M) seed/venture round, November 2025 - **Lead investors:** **Tesi** (Finland's sovereign investment fund) and **Nokia** - **What they do:** "Physical AI" for defence — builds NestOS, an open modular operating system for unmanned vehicles, autonomous operations, and command-and-control (C2) platforms. Founded by Peter Sarlin (ex-Silo AI/AMD). ### 2. Kova Labs (Helsinki, founded 2025) - **Round:** €1.5 million pre-seed, August 2025 - **Lead investors:** **Lifeline Ventures** and **Tuomas Rasila** - **What they do:** Vision-based autonomy for unmanned systems operating in GPS-denied, contested environments (forests, indoors, electronic-warfare zones). Works with the Finnish Defence Forces. ### 3. Sensofusion (Vantaa, founded 2016) - **Early funding:** €920K seed round, September 2024 - **Investors:** **FiBAN angels**, **Innovestor Angel Co-Fund**, and **Lifeline Ventures** - **What they do:** Counter-drone systems (AIRFENCE) — drone detection, signals intelligence, and electronic countermeasures for military and government customers. Now listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (IPO October 2026). ### 4. Kelluu (Joensuu, founded 2018) - **Round:** €15 million, 2026 - **Lead investor:** **NATO Innovation Fund** (its first Finnish investment) - **What they do:** Autonomous hydrogen-powered airships for ISR/surveillance. ### 5. Metaktik (Espoo, founded 2026) - **Round:** €1 million pre-seed, 2026 - **Lead investor:** **Maki.vc** - **What they do:** Ultra-light, flexible metasurface antennas for drones, satellites, and ground systems (comms, radar, stealth). Spin-out from Aalto University. ### 6. Securing seed backing requires technical differentiation in GPS-denied environments and trial validation with the Finnish Defence Forces or Border Guard (E4, E21).

committee.consensus: Conditional back: AeroRozum can raise €3M within 12 months if it targets unconflicted domestic VCs, proves GPS-denied autonomy, and secures pilot interest from Finnish defence stakeholders.

plan.verdict: AeroRozum faces tight seed benchmarks and incumbent airships; securing official Finnish Defence Forces trials is the vital lever to unlock three million euros.

drivers.name: Domestic Military and Border Guard Adoption
drivers.description: Official operational trials with Finnish Defence Forces or Border Guard establish necessary validation for seed investors.

drivers.name: Access to Pan-European and Sovereign Defence Capital
drivers.description: Capital availability from sovereign entities like Tesi and NATO Innovation Fund versus standard sub-two-million domestic seed checks.

drivers.name: Incumbent Dominance in Aerial Border Surveillance
drivers.description: Kelluu airships and Sensofusion counter-drone tech dominate Finnish border surveillance contracts and investor mindshare.

drivers.description: Typical Finnish defence pre-seed and seed rounds range from 920,000 to 1.5 million euros, making three million ambitious.

scenarios.name: Stalled Periphery
scenarios.oneLiner: Lacking defence validation and major funds, fundraising stalls well below target.
scenarios.narrative: Without Finnish Border Guard or Defence Forces engagement, local venture investors limit round sizes to sub-1.5 million euros, mirroring typical early Finnish seed tickets. AeroRozum cannot reach its three million euro target.
signposts: No trial agreements announced with the Finnish Border Guard.
VC term sheets capped below 1.5 million euros.

scenarios.name: Crowded Out By Giants
scenarios.oneLiner: Capital concentrates into established incumbents, bypassing unvalidated border surveillance startups.
scenarios.narrative: Heavy sovereign capital from Tesi and NATO Innovation Fund consolidates around proven leaders like Kelluu and NestAI. Without official procurement contracts, AeroRozum fails to convince institutional lead investors.
signposts: NATO Innovation Fund backs existing portfolio follow-on rounds.
Tier-one funds reject proposals lacking Finnish military trial data.

scenarios.name: Validated But Undersized
scenarios.oneLiner: Border trials succeed, but local syndicates cap seed checks below target.
scenarios.narrative: AeroRozum proves surveillance utility in border trials, but Finnish early-stage investors syndicate only one to two million euros. The startup must either downsize the round or defer remaining funding.
signposts: Announcement of Finnish Defence Forces innovation pilot.
Syndicate led by local angel funds offering under two million euros.

scenarios.name: Sovereign Fast Track
scenarios.oneLiner: Military validation unlocks a sovereign syndicate to fully fund three million euros.
scenarios.narrative: Endorsement through Finnish military surveillance trials mobilizes sovereign backing from Tesi, Lifeline, or NATO-aligned funds. AeroRozum successfully secures the full three million euro seed round within twelve months.
signposts: Joint operational trial with Finnish Border Guard or Defence Forces.
Co-investment term sheet from Tesi or NATO-associated venture partners.

event.question: Will AeroRozum close a seed round of about EUR 3,000,000 within 12 months?
event.explanation: AeroRozum aims to raise a EUR 3,000,000 seed round in Finland for border surveillance and defence logistics drones. While Finland captures 85 percent of Nordic defence investment, typical domestic seed rounds range from EUR 920,000 to EUR 1,500,000, and established competitors like Kelluu already hold major border surveillance backing.
